title: Implement Conditional Settlement Holds for Medium-Risk Transactions
description: The PayCircle Connect risk management team requires more granular control over transaction processing. Currently, the fraud detection service provides a binary outcome (approve/reject). This task introduces a third state for medium-risk transactions. Transactions flagged with `MEDIUM_RISK` by the `fraud_detection_service` should not be immediately settled or rejected. Instead, they must be placed in a new `PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW` state. Subsequently, a new administrative API must be created to allow an operator to manually approve or reject these held transactions. This feature will be implemented incrementally over three development sessions.

project_spec.name: PayCircle Connect
project_spec.description:
PayCircle Connect is a medium-scale fintech payment platform designed as a social-first money orbit where users form private ‘circles’ to pool, pay, lend, and settle funds together. Every function— from real-time multi-currency chat-payments to group-settlement challenges — is exposed through narrowly scoped C components running as independent micro-processes, enabling community-centric workflows such as shared KYC onboarding for clubs, co-operative fraud flagging, and crowd-auditable settlement trails.

Built around a rigorously component_based architecture, each capability (Audit Trail, KYC Verification, Fraud Detection, Encryption Gateway, Currency Router, Settlement Engine, etc.) is packaged as a plug-in shared library with a minimal C ABI and surfaced through gRPC gateways. Social constructs (circles, peer reputation scores, group spending limits) are persisted via CQRS, letting read-optimized community dashboards and write-secured payment flows scale independently. Audit logs stream in real-time to a public immutable ledger so circle members can socially validate every action, reinforcing trust while satisfying stringent regulatory_compliance requirements.
dependencies: glib >= 2.68 (event loop, data structures for component isolation)
sqlite3 >= 3.37 (lightweight CQRS command store per microservice)
libmnl + nftnl (optional kernel-level packet tagging for fraud heuristics)
